title: Разоблачение симулянта в палате  (Exposing the Faker in the Ward)

segments.t: At the hospital, Viktor Petrovich pretends to be unconscious so Elena Pavlovna will sit tenderly by his bedside and confess her feelings. His ward neighbor, however, mischievously ruins the act by casually mentioning that Spartak lost yesterday's match, causing Barinov to sit bolt upright.
Расскажите, как вы к нему относитесь.
А вы что, не в курсе?
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
Расскажите, как вы к нему относитесь.
'Tell him how you feel about him.' Barinov responds pointedly right here and reaches for the Russian word "otnosites" ("treat, handle", built from "otnositsya") right at the center of the line.

'Good morning, Viktor Petrovich!' Vika evenly extends this morning greeting in the exchange using "dobroye utro" ("good morning") — literally "kind morning", with the neuter ending matching "utro" ("morning").
'Did you watch the game yesterday?' Barinov inquires evenly why things suddenly took this turn between them.
'Very funny.' Vika opens up calmly on the spot and centers the remark on "smeshno" ("ridiculous") without any extra fuss.
'You are making fun of me.' Stepping in evenly in this beat, the "-sya" ending on "izdevayetes" ("are you mocking") marks an action that unfolds mutually or turns back on the speaker.

'Well, of course, for a long time now.' Vika firmly drops this confirmation to Barinov using "konechno" ("of course") — spoken with a soft "shn" sound in everyday Moscow Russian to mean "of course, certainly".
А вы что, не в курсе?
'Wait, did you not know?' Addressing the course in this beat, Barinov chooses "kurse" ("course, regimen", from the root "kurs") so Vika hears the exact meaning.
'Everything is fine already.' Holding firm warmly beside Barinov, spoken Russian drops "is" and "are" in the present, letting Vika place the two halves side by side.
'He is just sleeping.' Barinov jumps in calmly beside Vika, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
'How can that be?' Jumping in plainly beside Barinov, Vika puts the question word "kak" right at the start so Barinov hears the focus immediately.
'Just like that.' Turning readily to Vika, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'All right, enough, that is enough.' Vika weighs in honestly in this moment, before Barinov can change the subject.
'Everything is fine with me.' Barinov reacts vividly on the spot and lands on "normalno" ("fine, OK") as the key everyday word here.
Расскажите, как вы к нему относитесь.
А вы что, не в курсе?

That wraps up this scene as when Elena visits the hospital while Chef Barinov is pretending to be unconscious, his ward neighbor tricks Barinov into sitting bolt upright by mentioning Spartak's football match. Until next time!
